title: Exact sector structure pays for restricted loopy marginal completion
statement: On a connected simple qubit graph with at least3 vertices, Q_e=(I-Z_u Z_v)/2 and P_G=product(I-Q_e). Given PSD normalized single-site-consistent edge RDMs with EXACT Tr rho_e Q_e=0, a global extension exists iff every edge RDM equals the SAME p|00><00|+(1-p)|11><11|. Explicit global mixture and O(|E|) small-matrix/rational tests/compressed state; this is not arbitrary RDM compatibility. Pair Bell chain has individually zero defect and consistent I/2 singles but XX12=ZZ23=1 violates anticommuting squares<=1; necessary approximate bound |<XX12>|<=2sqrt(q(1-q)). For an ALREADY GLOBAL rho with TOTAL defect epsilon, projection to its normalized ground sector is within trace norm2sqrt(epsilon)+epsilon; no approximate arbitrary-RDM completion follows. On an L>=3 periodic square torus, H_t=sum_e Q_e(I-t X_u_e X_v_e), opposite-plaquette disjoint sites, |t|<1, has H_t>=(1-|t|)sum Q_e>=4(1-|t|)(I-P_G). Two product ground rays, exact long-range ZZ=1, e(h)=-|h| under Z source, and gap FLOOR4(1-|t|), not a measured gap. L3,t2/5 noncommuting exact fixture has commutator -8/5 and floor12/5. Sup |t_e|<1 allowed; arbitrary ground-sector perturbations/SU2 antiferromagnets not included. Ordinary local-projector domination proves the same control with less work. All admitted ferro-sector states have pair correlation+1/4, giving J1-J2 alpha.5 energy+.75 vs old upper-.46909: this exact sector cannot solve the actual Heisenberg target.

requires: Even periodic L square spin-1/2 J1-J2 at alpha=1/2; D_L=sum (-1)^x S_xy dot S_x+1,y; e(h)=lim lambda_min(H-hD)/L^2; m_D=-e-prime(0+). Observable norm density <=3/4. Positive m_D selects only columnar pi,0 bond order. Zero excludes only this component, not vertical/plaquette/topological/gapless alternatives.

Each positive control has its own exact sector/model assumptions; source-faithful quantum dimer basis is orthogonal and has specified positive rational edge amplitudes. Finite-field lower bound needs independently proved uniform field/volume curvature modulus.
